impacts.description: Improved researcher employability and career mobility within and beyond academia, contributing to a more dynamic and flexible research talent base in Europe.
impacts.source_section: Expected Outcome — For supported postdoctoral fellows
impacts.inference_note: The expected outcome states 'improved employability and career prospects of MSCA postdoctoral fellows within academia and beyond'. The broader societal impact — a more dynamic European research talent base — is directly derivable from this outcome as a systemic labour-market effect extending beyond individual fellows.

impacts.description: Enriched European R&I culture through the spread of international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary approaches and mind-sets, diversifying research methods and cross-boundary knowledge flows.
impacts.source_section: Expected Outcome — For supported postdoctoral fellows
impacts.inference_note: The expected outcome states 'new mind-sets and approaches to R&I work forged through international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience'. The broader scientific culture impact on the European R&I ecosystem is directly derivable from 'new mind-sets' as a systemic effect accumulating across supported fellows.

impacts.description: Increased societal engagement with and public understanding of research and innovation through enhanced researcher-to-public communication capacities and broadened Open Science practices.
impacts.source_section: Expected Outcome — For supported postdoctoral fellows
impacts.inference_note: The expected outcome states 'enhanced networking and communication capacities with scientific peers, as well as with the general public that will increase and broaden the research and innovation impact'. Broader societal engagement impact is derivable from the explicit 'general public' and 'broaden the research and innovation impact' phrasing in the source.

impacts.description: A more equitable and attractive European research environment through the progressive alignment of researcher working conditions with the European Charter for Researchers principles across participating organisations.
impacts.inference_note: The expected outcome states 'increased alignment of working conditions for researchers in accordance with the principles set out in the European Charter for Researchers'. The systemic policy impact on the European research environment is directly derivable from this organisational-level outcome scaled across participating organisations.

impacts.description: Strengthened European R&I competitiveness and global standing through the increased attractiveness, stronger knowledge output, and improved knowledge transfer capacity of participating research organisations.
impacts.inference_note: Derived from two co-located outcomes: 'increased global attractiveness, visibility and reputation of the participating organisation(s)' and 'stronger R&I capacity and output among participating organisations; better transfer of knowledge'. The broader economic competitiveness impact is directly derivable as a systemic aggregation of these organisational-level outcomes.

impacts.description: Enhanced knowledge circulation from the research system into education and society through the regular integration of R&I results into teaching at participating organisations.
impacts.inference_note: The expected outcome states 'regular feedback of research results into teaching and education at participating organisations'. The broader societal impact — knowledge circulation from the research sector into the education system — is directly derivable from this outcome as a systemic effect on the knowledge society.
